title: Distinction
summary: Reasoning begins by allowing one state, mark, or object to be told apart from another.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared preformal metalanguage context is fixed.

content.plain: Reasoning begins by allowing one state, mark, or object to be told apart from another.
content.exact: QEVA treats distinction as a declared primitive relation D(a,b) for a chosen context; it does not assert that one metaphysical notion of difference is forced on every framework.
content.example: The marks ○ and ● are distinguishable by fill in a visual encoding.
content.caveat: A distinction always depends on what an observer, test, language, or structure can detect.
